flow_overview: A passenger facing rail travel website that lets users browse onboard travel information and reach dining menu resources through a hierarchical content flow.
capability_summary: Top level browsing of travel experience content
Hierarchical navigation through onboard amenities and services
Access to national and route specific café menu resources
Contextual side navigation and section wayfinding

requirements.text: The system shall present sample menu resources from the café service page.
requirements.rationale: The Café page presents sample menu resources as requested.

claims.claim: Sample menu resources are presented from the café service page.
claims.claim_text: Sample menu resources are presented from the café service page.

requirements.evidence_note: Step 5 shows a Sample Menus section with National and Regional menu resources.

requirements.text: The system shall preserve contextual wayfinding by indicating the current section and subsection as users navigate deeper into onboard content.
requirements.rationale: The visible navigation state preserves contextual wayfinding through the section and subsection hierarchy.

claims.claim: The current section is indicated as users navigate deeper into onboard content.
claims.claim_text: The current section is indicated as users navigate deeper into onboard content.

claims.claim: The current subsection is indicated as users navigate deeper into onboard content.
claims.claim_text: The current subsection is indicated as users navigate deeper into onboard content.

requirements.evidence_note: The left navigation persists across the Onboard, Onboard Dining, and Café states. Onboard Dining and Café are highlighted as the flow moves deeper.

requirements.text: The system shall allow travelers to open the national café menu in a dedicated resource that can be viewed independently of the surrounding café information page.
requirements.rationale: The access point is supported, while the dedicated independent viewing outcome is not shown.
requirements.parent_harvest_text: The system shall provide access to a national café menu.

claims.claim: Access to the national café menu is provided.
claims.claim_text: Access to the national café menu is provided.

claims.claim: Travelers can open the national café menu in a dedicated resource.
claims.claim_text: Travelers can open the national café menu in a dedicated resource.

claims.claim: The dedicated resource can be viewed independently of the surrounding café information page.
claims.claim_text: The dedicated resource can be viewed independently of the surrounding café information page.

requirements.evidence_note: Step 5 shows the National Café Menu link, but the flow does not show the menu resource being opened or viewed independently.

requirements.text: The system shall make onboard dining menu resources reachable to public users without requiring sign-in or account ownership checks.
requirements.rationale: Public reachability and absence of a visible sign-in step are supported, but the no-account-ownership-check condition remains hidden.
requirements.parent_harvest_text: The system shall make onboard dining information discoverable through the public site navigation without requiring the user to enter a booking flow first.

claims.claim: Onboard dining menu resources are reachable to public users.
claims.claim_text: Onboard dining menu resources are reachable to public users.

claims.claim: Reachability of onboard dining menu resources does not require sign-in before access.
claims.claim_text: Reachability of onboard dining menu resources does not require sign-in before access.

claims.claim: Reachability of onboard dining menu resources does not require account ownership checks.
claims.claim_text: Reachability of onboard dining menu resources does not require account ownership checks.

requirements.evidence_note: Steps 1 to 5 reach the Café page and menu links through public navigation without a visible sign-in step. The linked menu resources themselves are not opened, and account-ownership-check behavior is not verifiable from the screenshots.

requirements.text: The system shall surface route-specific café menu resources only when they are applicable to the traveler's route or service context, while still preserving access to a general national menu.
requirements.rationale: The national-menu portion is supported, while the route-applicability condition depends on context and logic not shown in the flow.
requirements.parent_harvest_text: The system shall provide route or region specific café menu resources in addition to a national menu.

claims.claim: Access to a general national café menu is preserved.
claims.claim_text: Access to a general national café menu is preserved.

claims.claim: Route-specific café menu resources are surfaced only when applicable to the traveler's route or service context.
claims.claim_text: Route-specific café menu resources are surfaced only when applicable to the traveler's route or service context.

requirements.evidence_note: Step 5 preserves a National Café Menu and also lists Regional menu links. No traveler route or service context is shown, so applicability of the route-specific resources cannot be judged.

requirements.text: The system shall provide corresponding detail or menu-entry resources for all dining service types presented from the onboard dining page.
requirements.rationale: The requirement asks for corresponding detail or menu-entry resources. The visible dining entries and Café detail path support that mechanism for the presented types.
requirements.parent_harvest_text: The system shall support drill down within onboard dining into specific dining service types such as traditional dining, flexible dining, café dining, and Acela dining.

claims.claim: Dining service types are presented from the onboard dining page.
claims.claim_text: Dining service types are presented from the onboard dining page.

claims.claim: Corresponding detail or menu-entry resources are provided for all presented dining service types.
claims.claim_text: Corresponding detail or menu-entry resources are provided for all presented dining service types.

requirements.evidence_note: Step 4 presents Traditional Dining, Flexible Dining, Café, and Acela Dining as dining service type entries. Step 5 demonstrates the Café detail path and menu-entry resources.

requirements.text: The system shall present an intermediate menu selection step that clearly separates national café menu access from route-specific menu access before the user opens a menu resource.
requirements.rationale: The visible Café menu-selection state clearly separates national and regional menu access before any menu resource is opened.
requirements.parent_harvest_text: The system shall provide route or region specific café menu resources in addition to a national menu.

claims.claim: An intermediate menu selection step is presented before a menu resource is opened.
claims.claim_text: An intermediate menu selection step is presented before a menu resource is opened.

claims.claim: National café menu access and route-specific menu access are clearly separated before a menu resource is opened.
claims.claim_text: National café menu access and route-specific menu access are clearly separated before a menu resource is opened.

requirements.evidence_note: Step 5 shows a Sample Menus area before any menu resource is opened, with a National grouping and a Regional grouping.

requirements.text: The system shall maintain consistent dining subtype naming and menu-resource terminology from the onboard dining overview through the café detail page so users can easily match the selected dining model to its menu links.
requirements.rationale: Subtype naming is supported, while the full terminology-consistency claim remains ambiguous.
requirements.parent_harvest_text: The system shall present menu options for multiple onboard dining formats so travelers can distinguish among dining models before selecting a menu resource.

claims.claim: Dining subtype naming is maintained from the onboard dining overview through café detail content.
claims.claim_text: Dining subtype naming is maintained from the onboard dining overview through café detail content.

claims.claim: Menu-resource terminology consistently supports matching the selected dining model to its menu links.
claims.claim_text: Menu-resource terminology consistently supports matching the selected dining model to its menu links.

requirements.evidence_note: The Café subtype name remains consistent from step 4 to step 5. Some menu links in step 5 are named by route or service, so the consistency of every menu-resource label with the Café model is interpretive.
